result.title: From Clips to Streams: A Unified Framework for Streaming Sign Language Translation
result.comment: 27 pages, 7 figures, the paper has been accepted to NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Sign Language Translation (SLT) research has typically focused on pre-segmented clips, a constraint that disconnects models from the continuous reality of real-world communication. To bridge the gap from clips to streams, we formally define Streaming SLT, a realistic task demanding the joint discovery and translation of linguistic events from continuous, untrimmed video inputs. To address this challenge, we propose StreamSLST, the first end-to-end framework for Streaming Sign Language Segmentation and Translation via Deformable Transformer architecture. Unlike cascaded approaches that suffer from error propagation, StreamSLST employs a parallel decoding strategy to jointly optimize temporal segmentation and translation in a single pass. To enable scalable training on long-form videos, we incorporate a Sentence-aware Sliding Window Sampler that crops continuous streams into trainable units. We further design a Tri-modal Visual-Language Pretraining stage that aligns pose dynamics with textual semantics before joint optimization. To support comprehensive evaluation, we conduct experiments on two real-world streaming datasets, BOBSL and How2Sign, together with two newly constructed synthetic streaming benchmarks, Streaming-Phoenix-2014T and Streaming-CSL-Daily. The results demonstrate that StreamSLST consistently outperforms a matched cascaded segmentation-then-translation pipeline. Interestingly, our analysis reveals that joint optimization learns wider, translation-effective temporal support that simple expansion or rescaling of the annotated spans fails to reproduce. Our work establishes the first robust benchmark for continuous sign language understanding and paves the way for accessible real-world communication interfaces. The source code and data are available at https://github.com/streamsl/StreamSLST.

AI.brief_summary: 论文形式化定义「流式手语翻译」任务，并提出 StreamSLST：基于 Deformable Transformer 在单次前向中并行解码时间分割与翻译，配合句子感知滑动窗口采样和三模态视觉-语言预训练，在真实与合成流式基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「联合优化学到更宽且对翻译有效的时间支撑」的分析与并行解码结构，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、LOOK 窗口范围和贡献分配提供可供核查的线索，但任务本身是连续翻译而非推理。
